result.title: bf16 Rounding Silently Discards Most RL Policy Updates: A Hidden Training-Inference Mismatch and an Unbiased One-Line Fix
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training of language models keeps fp32 master weights in the optimizer and serves rollouts from a bf16 copy produced by round-to-nearest conversion. At the learning rates in common use, most per-step updates are smaller than half a bf16 spacing and the conversion discards them: on Qwen3-1.7B only 0.4-0.5% of served weights change per step, and the policy that generates the training data lags the optimizer by 50-150 steps. Existing mismatch corrections cannot see this lag because they compare two copies downstream of the same rounding. We propose Fair Cast: export the master with an unbiased rounding rule (stochastic rounding or error feedback) and compute the training loss on the served copy. The change is one line at the export call, adds no hyperparameters and costs 22-38 ms per export of 1.7B parameters. Across 25 matched seed-pairs on Qwen3-0.6B to 4B with AdamW and Muon, Fair Cast is ahead on 18, tied on 6 and behind on 1, with a mean gain of 6.1 points; on zebra puzzles it reaches 0.57 +/- 0.16 over four runs where round-to-nearest collapses to 0.33 +/- 0.10. It also makes the saved fp32 checkpoint agree with the served model, and it exposes the implicit lag of round-to-nearest as a regularizer that can be restored explicitly when a task needs it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出 bf16 导出把大多数小于半个 bf16 间距的 RL 权重更新静默丢弃，使采样策略滞后优化器 50–150 步；提出 Fair Cast，在导出时改用随机舍入或误差反馈并在服务副本上算损失，在 Qwen3-0.6B–4B 上取得平均 6.1 点提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「低精度转换丢弃微小状态更新、训练副本与推理副本隐式不一致」的度量与无偏舍入/误差反馈思路，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态、KV 缓存与深度/位置相似度实验是否被数值舍入掩盖了真实更新。
